Palladium-catalyzed asymmetric propargylic
sulfonylation of propargyl esters with sulfonyl
hydrazides
Zhi-Xiong Ou, Bu-Hong Zhang, Jia-Xin Song, Li-Bo Li and Xing-Wang Wang
 *
Palladium-catalyzed enantioselective propargylic sulfonylation
between racemic propargyl esters and readily available sulfonyl
hydrazides with an N-benzylamino-bridged bidentate phosphora-
midite ( N-Bn-Me-BIPAM) ligand was reported. The corresponding
reactions provided a series of enantiomerically rich propargylic
sulfones in good yields with high enantioselectivity under mild
reaction conditions.
1. Introduction
Sulfonyl (R-SO 2-R) backbones endowed with distinct electronic
and structural features are versatile synthetic intermediates in
organic chemistry. 1 As a result, sulfone compounds were
widely found in many target molecules of importance in syn-
thetic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, agricultural chemistry,
and materials science. 2 The sulfone moiety enhances the
eﬃcacy and potency of a drug molecule by forming strong
hydrogen bonds with a biological target. 3 Therefore, sulfones
not only serve as important building blocks in numerous
medicines and drug candidates and natural products, but also
play important roles in the discovery of new anticancer agents,
antibacterial agents, insecticides and herbicides.
4 In the past
few decades, great progress has been made in the synthesis of
sulfonyl compounds, and a variety of novel organo- and metal-
catalyzed methods have been established. 5 Among these
methods, the development of e ﬃcient and practical synthetic
methods for chiral sulfones has attracted significant interest
from synthetic chemists.6
Alkynyl sulfones are sulfone derivatives that show very
important synthetic utility and are crucial structural moieties
that are present in some pharmaceutically and biologically active
molecules, such as the inhibitors of cathepsins, cancer Osaka
thyroid kinase modulators, DNA cleaving agents, etc. (Fig. 1).
7
The synthesis of propargyl sulfone backbones has attracted
increased attention due to the increase in use,8 and correspond-
ingly some e ﬃcient methods were reported to synthesize the
target molecules.9,10 From 2018, several groups constructed pro-
pargyl sulfones under metal-free conditions in good to high
yields using methods which utilized propargyl alcohols with sul-
finic acids, sodium sulfites or sulfinamides as sulfone sources
(Scheme 1a, i–iii).
11–13 Meanwhile, the Lian group reported a pal-
ladium-catalyzed multicomponent cross-electrophilic coupling
reaction from propargyl acetates, aryl iodides and DABSO to
furnish propargyl sulfones in moderate to high yields
(Scheme 1b, i).
14 Kleij and Wu reported enantioselective sulfony-
lation through a copper-catalyzed two-component reaction of
propargylic cyclic carbonates with sodium sulfinates or through
a three-component reaction of propargylic cyclic carbonates,
cyclopropan-1-ols and DABCO·(SO
2)2, allowing the preparation
of tertiary terminal propargylic sulfones with quaternary stereo-
centers in excellent ee values (Scheme 1b, ii).15 According to pre-
vious literature reports, 16 the transition metal-catalyzed de-
carboxylation of propargylic carbonates delivers either a metal-
propargyl intermediate or a metal-allenyl species. Then, the

or metal-allenyl intermediate provides a stereoselective route to

(Scheme 1c).
Herein, we reported a bidentate phosphoramidite-Pd
complex-catalyzed asymmetric transformation for the syn-
thesis of chiral propargylic sulfones using propargyl esters
with commercially available sulfonyl hydrazides. A series of
enantioenriched propargylic sulfones were a ﬀorded under
mild reaction conditions in moderate yields with good
enantioselectivity, highlighting the potential utility of this syn-
thetic method (Scheme 1d).
2. Results and discussion
We commenced the study with the palladium-catalyzed asym-
metric propargylic sulfonylation of racemic tert-butoxypropar-
gyl ester 1a with commercially available p-toluenesulfonyl
hydrazide 2a. A series of BINOL-derived monodentate and
bidentate phosphoramidite ligands L1–L9 were initially tested
with 5 mol% of Pd
2(dba)3 and 5 mol% of MnO 2 as the oxidant.
The catalytic results are presented in Table 1 (see SI for full
ligand screening results). For monodentate phosphoramidite
ligands L1–L5, all reactions gave product 3 with less than 58%
ee (Table 1, entries 1 –5). However, when the bidentate phos-
phoramidite (Me-Bipam) ligand L6 was used, the corres-
ponding chiral propargyl sulfone 3 was a ﬀorded in 82% ee,
albeit in a 17% yield (Table 1, entry 6). Therefore, inspired by
this promising result and guided by previous work by
Miyaura’s group on Me-Bipam ligands,
17 some new chiral
bidentate phosphoramidite ligands L7–L9 bearing bridged
benzylamino groups were synthesized. When the ligands
L7–L9 were employed for the reaction, it was found that the
product 3 was obtained in 24 –55% yield with 54 –79% ee
values (Table 1, entries 7 –9). Of the bidentate phosphoramidite
ligands tested, the N-Bn-Me-BIPAM ligand L7 with a bridged
benzylamino group turned out to be optimal for this trans-

With the optimized chiral ligand L7 in hand, several other
parameters, such as the metal precursor, reaction media, reac-
tion temperature and oxidants, were further explored for the
reaction, and the experimental results are summarized in
Table 2. Initially, some Pd(0) precursors, including Pd
2(dba)3,
Pd2(dba)3·CHCl3 and Pd(PPh 3)4, were examined, and the
corresponding reactions a ﬀorded the target compound 3 in
29–55% yield with 53 –79% ee values (Table 2, entries 1 –3). In
contrast, other metal precursors and Pd(OAc) 2 showed no reac-
tivity under these reaction conditions (Table 2, entry 4, also
see SI for details). Then, several other types of common
organic solvents were evaluated for the reaction (Table 2,
entries 5 –7, see SI for details). THF was the optimal reaction
medium for this reaction. Subsequently, the influence of reac-
tion temperature was examined. The reactivity showed a sig-
nificant temperature dependence, while the enantioselectivity
varied modestly (Table 2, entries 5, 8 –10). It was found that
80 °C was optimal for the reaction. Di ﬀerent oxidants signifi-
cantly a ﬀected both the reactivity and enantioselectivity
(Table 2, entries 11 –14). Notably, the use of air as the oxidant
aﬀorded the target product 3 in 65% yield with 89% ee value
(Table 2, entry 13). Based on its a ﬀordability, eco-friendly
nature and excellent performance, air was selected as the
oxidant for further reactions (see SI for details). When 2,4,6-
triisopropylbenzenesulfonyl hydrazide 2b was employed as a
sulfonyl source, the desired product 4 was obtained in 65%
yield with a 93% ee value (Table 2, entry 15, see SI for more
details). Finally, the optimized reaction conditions were estab-
lished in the presence of 5.0 mol% of Pd
2(dba)3 and 6.0 mol%
of ligand L7 with air as the oxidant and a substrate ratio of
1a : 2b of 1.2 : 1 in THF at 80 °C.
With the optimized reaction conditions established, the sub-
strate scope of various aryl-substituted propargyl esters 1a–1n
in the reaction with 2b was investigated. The corresponding
chiral propargyl sulfones 4–17 were obtained in 47 –65% yields
with 55 –93% ee values. The results are shown in Scheme 2.
For the reaction of phenyl-substituted propargyl ester 1a with
2b, the product 4 was obtained in 65% yield with a 93% ee
value. When the substrates 1b–1d with –F, –Cl and –Br groups
at the para-positions of the phenyl rings were investigated for
the reaction, the desired products 5–7 were isolated in 47 –60%
yields, all with 92% ee values. Then, substrates 1e and 1f with
–Cl and –OCF3 groups at the meta-positions of the phenyl
rings were utilized for the reaction, and the corresponding pro-
ducts 8 and 9 were delivered in 55% and 47% yields with 78%
and 60% ee values, respectively. For substrate 1g with a para-
trifluoromethoxy group, the corresponding reaction furnished
the desired product 10 in 50% yield with an 80% ee value. On
the other hand, substrates 1h–1k with electron-donating sub-
stituents of –OMe, –OEt, –Me, –tBu at the para-positions of the
phenyl rings were employed for the reaction and provided the
corresponding products 11–14 in 47 –54% yields with 55 –89%
ee values, respectively. For the ortho-Me-substituted phenyl
propargyl ester 1l, the reaction produced the desire product 15
in 58% yield with 89% ee. Moreover, substrates 1m and 1n di-
substituted with methyl groups were also suitable for this reac-
tion, and the corresponding products 16 and 17 were respect-

To gain insight into the possible coordination mode by
which the chiral N-Bn-Me-BIPAM ligand L7 and Pd 2(dba)3
form the catalytically active species in the reaction, a nonlinear
eﬀects study 18 was carried out on the Pd-catalyzed sulfonyla-
tion of propargyl carbonate 1c with sulfonyl hydrazide 2b
under the optimized reaction conditions. As shown in
Scheme 5, the enantiopurity of product 6 displays a linear
relationship with the blend of L7 and ent-L7 that is used,
which indicates that a palladium center likely coordinates with
a single ligand unit.
On the basis of the control experiments and previous litera-
ture reports, we proposed a mechanism
19 for this propargylic
sulfonylation, as shown in Scheme 6. Initially, complex A of
Pd0L* is coordinated with the triple bond of propargylic car-
bonate 1 to form complex B, which undergoes oxidative
addition with propargylic carbonate 1 to form zwitterionic pro-
pargyl Pd II intermediate C via the elimination of carbon
dioxide. The sulfonyl hydrazide 2 is then deprotonated by a
tert-butoxide ion and is subsequently oxidized to produce the
sulfinate anion (ArSO 2
−) with the release of N 2 and H 2O. The
resulting Pd IIL*-propargylic sulfinate (ArSO 2
−) D undergoes a
reductive elimination to form the corresponding propargyl
sulfone products. Simultaneously, the catalyst is regenerated
for the next catalytic cycle.
3. Conclusions
In summary, palladium-catalyzed enantioselective sulfonyla-
tion of propargyl carbonates with sulfonyl hydrazides that uti-
lizes a chiral N-Bn-Me-BIPAM ligand under mild reaction con-
ditions was developed. This reaction delivered the corres-
ponding propargyl sulfones in good yields with high enantio-
selectivity. Meanwhile, this transformation has good func-
tional group tolerance, a wide substrate scope, as well as good
atom and step economy. It is noteworthy that the employment
of air as a promoter ensures the reactivity and delivers optimal
catalytic results. Further e ﬀorts in our laboratory are focused
on expanding the stereoselective transformation of propargyl
carbonates into a practical catalytic system.
4. Experimental section
General procedure for the synthesis of the chiral propargyl
sulfones.
In a tube, Pd 2(dba)3 (4.5 mg, 0.005 mmol) and L7 (5.1 mg,
0.006 mmol) were added to anhydrous THF (2.0 ml) under a
nitrogen atmosphere. The mixture was stirred for 0.5 hours at
room temperature to produce a bright yellow solution. Under
an air atmosphere, various substituted propargyl esters
(0.12 mmol) and substituted sulfonyl hydrazides (0.10 mmol)
were added at 25 °C. Then, the resulting mixture was stirred in
an oil bath at 80 °C for 12 hours. After the reaction was com-
plete (monitored by TLC), it was subjected to silica gel column
chromatography to aﬀord the desired products.

Palladium-catalyzed asymmetric propargylic
sulfonylation of propargyl esters with sulfonyl
hydrazides
Zhi-Xiong Ou, Bu-Hong Zhang, Jia-Xin Song, Li-Bo Li and Xing-Wang Wang *
rsc.li/obc

Palladium-catalyzed enantioselective propargylic sulfonylation
between racemic propargyl esters and readily available sulfonyl
hydrazides with an N-benzylamino-bridged bidentate phosphora-
midite (N-Bn-Me-BIPAM) ligand was reported. The corresponding
reactions provided a series of enantiomerically rich propargylic
sulfones in good yields with high enantioselectivity under mild
reaction conditions.
1. Introduction

Sulfonyl
\left( \mathbf { R } { - } \mathbf { S } \mathbf { O } _ { 2 } { - } \mathbf { R } \right)
backbones endowed with distinct electronic
and structural features are versatile synthetic intermediates in
organic chemistry.<sup>1</sup> As a result, sulfone compounds were
widely found in many target molecules of importance in syn-
thetic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, agricultural chemistry,
and materials science.<sup>2</sup> The sulfone moiety enhances the
eficacy and potency of a drug molecule by forming strong
hydrogen bonds with a biological target.<sup>3</sup> Therefore, sulfones
not only serve as important building blocks in numerous
medicines and drug candidates and natural products, but also
play important roles in the discovery of new anticancer agents,
antibacterial agents, insecticides and herbicides.<sup>4</sup> In the past
few decades, great progress has been made in the synthesis of
sulfonyl compounds, and a variety of novel organo- and metal-
catalyzed methods have been established.<sup>5</sup> Among these
methods, the development of eficient and practical synthetic
methods for chiral sulfones has attracted significant interest
from synthetic chemists.<sup>6</sup>

Alkynyl sulfones are sulfone derivatives that show very
important synthetic utility and are crucial structural moieties
that are present in some pharmaceutically and biologically active
molecules, such as the inhibitors of cathepsins, cancer Osaka
thyroid kinase modulators, DNA cleaving agents, etc. (Fig. 1).<sup>7</sup>

The synthesis of propargyl sulfone backbones has attracted
increased attention due to the increase in use,<sup>8</sup> and correspond-
ingly some eficient methods were reported to synthesize the
target molecules.<sup>9,10</sup> From 2018, several groups constructed pro-
pargyl sulfones under metal-free conditions in good to high
yields using methods which utilized propargyl alcohols with sul-
finic acids, sodium sulfites or sulfinamides as sulfone sources
(Scheme 1a, i–iii).<sup>11–13</sup> Meanwhile, the Lian group reported a pal-
ladium-catalyzed multicomponent cross-electrophilic coupling
reaction from propargyl acetates, aryl iodides and DABSO to
furnish propargyl sulfones in moderate to high yields
(Scheme 1b, i).<sup>14</sup> Kleij and Wu reported enantioselective sulfony-
lation through a copper-catalyzed two-component reaction of
propargylic cyclic carbonates with sodium sulfinates or through
a three-component reaction of propargylic cyclic carbonates,
cyclopropan-1-ols and

of tertiary terminal propargylic sulfones with quaternary stereo-

vious literature reports,<sup>16</sup> the transition metal-catalyzed de-
carboxylation of propargylic carbonates delivers either a metal-

Herein, we reported a bidentate phosphoramidite-Pd

3. Conclusions

In summary, palladium-catalyzed enantioselective sulfonyla-
tion of propargyl carbonates with sulfonyl hydrazides that uti-
lizes a chiral N-Bn-Me-BIPAM ligand under mild reaction con-
ditions was developed. This reaction delivered the corres-
ponding propargyl sulfones in good yields with high enantio-
selectivity. Meanwhile, this transformation has good func-
tional group tolerance, a wide substrate scope, as well as good
atom and step economy. It is noteworthy that the employment
of air as a promoter ensures the reactivity and delivers optimal
catalytic results. Further eforts in our laboratory are focused
on expanding the stereoselective transformation of propargyl
carbonates into a practical catalytic system.
